clockPolicy: Only facts with known safe availability at or before asOf are input. Date-only sources use conservative bounds. Unknown original availability is explicit; later revisions cannot be backdated.
sourceBodyPolicy: Only factual paraphrases and source links retained. No full external page, personal contacts, photo or logo asset is copied.

cases.title: A strong jobs headline misses a sudden contraction

preAsOfFacts.paraphrase: February total nonfarm employment increased by 273,000; unemployment was 3.5%.

authoredPrediction.target: March 2020 US total nonfarm payroll employment change, in the first BLS release, is below zero.
authoredPrediction.windowMeaning: Target reference period or event deadline; distinct from later publication/reveal clock.
authoredPrediction.severity: Illustrative material exposure; not a quantified organization loss.
authoredPrediction.rationale: An intentionally weak persistence method treats the latest positive payroll headline as dominant. This retrospective authored estimate uses only the stated February release.

outcome.revealBasis: Only reveal after all retained outcome facts are safely publicly available.

facts.paraphrase: The April 3 release reported a March payroll decline of 701,000.

evaluation.leadTimeBasis: A precise physical-risk onset is not established. Hourly risk-warning lead time is therefore unknown.
evaluation.publicationLeadLabel: Time from replay cutoff to safe public reveal. This is not physical-risk warning lead time.

The employment survey measures a reference pay period including the12th, not daily onset. The prediction object is the first release vintage.

learningStep.error: Miss: the locked 25% forecast did not raise an alert at the fixed 50% threshold.
learningStep.attribution: Authored demonstration diagnosis, not a proven causal explanation of the historical event.
learningStep.methodologyUpdate: Require a freshness/coverage check and explicit missing-event-evidence state before treating a monthly headline as a current operating signal. Add timely sources only if they were already public at the new cutoff.
